title: Lysozyme-based removal of bacteria from cultures of Cafeteria roenbergensis
author: Monica Berjon-Otero
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.88ihzue

steps.title: Determine initial cell density
steps.instruction: Determine the cell density of Cafeteria roenbergensis using a haemocytometer (Neubauer Chamber).

substeps.instruction: Stain 10 µL of Cafeteria culture with 1 µL of Lugol’s acid iodine solution.

steps.title: Dilute and incubate culture
steps.instruction: Dilute the Cafeteria culture to 5 x 10^5 cells/mL using f/2 medium supplemented with 0.03% (w/v) yeast extract.

steps.title: Harvest flagellates
steps.instruction: Prepare approximately 8 x 10^7 Cafeteria cells per sample by centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge flagellates in 50 mL Falcon tubes at 4,500 g for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Resuspend cell pellets
steps.instruction: Resuspend the resulting cell pellets in 1.8 mL of 1X PBS and transfer them into 2 mL microfuge tubes.

steps.title: Treat with lysozyme
steps.instruction: Add 40 μL of freshly prepared 50 mg/mL lysozyme in 1X PBS to achieve a final concentration of 1 mg/mL.

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Optionally add 5 mM EDTA to increase lysozyme activity against Gram negative bacteria (note: this may negatively affect Cafeteria mobility).

steps.title: Treat with DNaseI
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of freshly prepared 10 mg/mL DNaseI in 1X PBS (1 mg/mL final concentration, 2 U/µL) and 11 µL of 1M MgCl2 (5 mM final concentration).

substeps.instruction: Incubate for 30 min at 34°C in a thermomixer with shaking.

steps.title: Centrifuge treated cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the sample at 5,000 g for 6 min at 20°C.

steps.title: Prepare for gradient loading
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellets in 100 µL of 1X gradient buffer (0.5 M NaCl in 1X PBS).

substeps.instruction: Pipette up and down several times to break up aggregates.
Add 1X gradient buffer to reach a final resuspended cell volume of 0.5 - 1 mL (up to 1 x 10^9 Cafeteria cells can be loaded per SW28 centrifuge tube).

steps.title: Load Optiprep gradient
steps.instruction: Load the sample on top of a two-step Optiprep cushion in an SW28 centrifuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Place 20% (w/v) Optiprep at the bottom of the tube.
Layer 10% (w/v) Optiprep on top of the 20% layer (both solutions prepared in 1X gradient buffer).

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge sample
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes in a Beckman SW28 rotor ultracentrifuge at 20,000 g for 20 min at 20°C using slow braking.

steps.title: Recover Cafeteria cells
steps.instruction: Recover Cafeteria cells from the interphase between the 10% and 20% Optiprep layers.

steps.title: Wash and dilute cells
steps.instruction: Dilute the recovered Cafeteria cells at least twofold with F/2 medium (without yeast extract).

substeps.instruction: If no or little dilution is required, centrifuge again for 6 min at 5,000 g at 20°C and resuspend in F/2 to remove remaining Optiprep.

steps.title: Quantify cells and bacteria
steps.instruction: Quantify Cafeteria cells and remaining bacteria using a haemocytometer.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the culture 25-fold or 50-fold with F/2.
Stain 10 µL of this dilution with 1 µL of Lugol’s acid iodine solution.

steps.title: Final density adjustment
steps.instruction: Dilute Cafeteria cells to the desired final density.
